topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture series, outlines the topic of cancer causation, and presents the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cancer causation, endogenous versus environmental risk, and geographic incidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multifaceted origins of cancer, contrasting intrinsic mutational processes with environmental exposures and global epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral mechanisms in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on how pathogens contribute to malignancy, examining specific mechanisms and the co-infection model of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens, metabolic activation, and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe specific dietary, environmental, and chemical mutagens and the metabolic processes by which they cause DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, chronic inflammation, and host susceptibility windows
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of cancer development, including chronic inflammation, the initiator-promoter model, and host developmental timing.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail experimental, genomic, and epidemiological approaches used to detect mutagenicity and prove carcinogenicity, concluding with risk-benefit considerations.
